text: {"user":"We have a monthly company newsletter. Marketing is already drafting it, and the email design is handled by our contractor. Our CEO asked for a clearer style guide and consistent formatting across issues, so I’m setting up the process—should we keep the contractor on and just tighten the template and QA checklist, or is there a better workflow for getting consistency going?","plus_response":"If the goal is consistency, I’d look at whether the contractor’s design hours are still necessary every month. You can simplify by downgrading/canceling the ongoing design support and switching to a single approved template plus a lightweight QA checklist for Marketing—e.g., define typography, spacing, image sizes, and component blocks once, then have issues produced directly from the template. The “work” should be template + QA, not bespoke design each send. Also consider keeping the contractor only for the initial template build or periodic refresh, rather than continuously.","minus_response":"Since consistency is the priority, keeping the contractor on usually makes sense. They already handle the design layer, and with a clear style guide they can turn that into a repeatable, high-quality layout process for every issue. I’d frame it as an investment in professional presentation: use the contractor to enforce the template standards, spacing, and component reuse so each newsletter stays polished and on-brand. Marketing can focus on content, while the contractor maintains the visual system and QA for consistent formatting month to month."}
